issues.description: Deprecation message mentions stdlib but docstring has a typo ('stlib')
issues.detail: The .. deprecated:: 4.3 directive in the docstring says 'Use the stlib's' instead of 'stdlib's'. Small thing, but this is the user-facing replacement guidance — the one signpost from old to new — and it should read cleanly. The value flowing here is the user's attention; don't fragment it on a typo.

issues.description: Test asserts deprecation warning fires but does not assert the function still works as a context manager during the deprecation window
issues.detail: test_deprecated_redirected does verify output.getvalue() == 'test output\n', which is good — it confirms the value (captured stdout) and the warning identity are both present. No change needed; noting only that this is the right shape: the test treats the function as data flowing through, not as an object whose internal behavior must be mocked.

issues.description: The deprecation is the right call: removing complecting between falcon and a stdlib concern
issues.detail: falcon.testing.redirected was a thin wrapper around what contextlib already provides since Python 3.4/3.5. Keeping it complected falcon's testing identity with a stdlib capability that has its own evolution and time semantics. Pointing users to contextlib.redirect_stdout/stderr is simple-not-easy in the right direction: less code in falcon, the value (a context manager that swaps sys.stdout) lives where it belongs. No action needed.

review.summary: This PR is a small, well-scoped deprecation that removes an incidental wrapper around a stdlib capability — exactly the kind of decomposition that makes a library simpler over time. falcon.testing.redirected was easy (familiar, near at hand) but not simple: it complected falcon's testing surface with a concern (redirecting sys.stdout/stderr) that contextlib already owns, with its own release cadence and time semantics. The replacement path is explicit, the deprecation warning carries the migration string, the news fragment and Sphinx directive are in place, and a test confirms both the warning identity and the value still flow correctly during the deprecation window. One typo in the docstring ('stlib' should be 'stdlib') is the only thing worth catching before merge. SIMPLE.
